title: Option drag on a clip leaves a copy behind
goal: Holding Option while dragging a clip along the timeline should drag out a copy and leave the original where it was, as it does in Premiere, Final Cut and on Photonz's own canvas. Today Option on the timeline only draws a range, so an editor's first reflex for reusing a piece does nothing they expect.
notes: Lane press: TimelineTrackRows.swift:965-990 uses Option to start a range on empty space (drawsRange). Clip bar drag: Sources/PhotonzCore/ClipBarDrag.swift + Sources/Photonz/EditorState+ClipBar.swift have no modifier handling at all (grep option/modifierFlags finds nothing). Option-copy already exists on the canvas and in key lanes; match its cursor. Duplicate (Command J) already exists in the clip menu (EditorState+TimelineMenus.swift:213) for the copy itself. Found by the 2026-10-05 evening manager pass's key audit.
acceptance: Option and drag on a clip's bar moves a copy (with its linked sound) to where you let go, snapping as a plain drag does, and the original stays put; one undo removes the copy
Option and drag on EMPTY track space still draws a range, as today
The pointer shows the copy cursor while Option is held over a clip, the same as the canvas's Option drag
A walk at Next defaults Option-drags a clip to a later moment and checks there are two clips with the same source; it runs green
Try it: open a recording, split it with B, hold Option and drag the second piece to the right. Audit written under queue/audits/
anything left rough is filed as a follow-up task if it clears the follow-up bar, and written into this task's log if it does not

log.note: Before building: after a split the clip is ONE layer of two pieces, so Option on a piece has to copy that piece as a clip of its own (an editor sees each stretch between cuts as a clip). A copy that lands over something on its own track would put two clips on one moment of one track, which no editor allows, so it goes up onto a new track over it, the rule paste-at-playhead landed today. On the timeline the split key is Command K (B picks the Blade, Premiere's way), so the audit says Command K, not the B the task text assumed.

Built: core ClipDragCopy.swift (clipDragCopy, placeClipCopy, liftClipsOffOverlaps with a track id derived from the copy so preview and drop share one row) + 15 tests; EditorState+ClipBar copy session (made at the grab, drawn in the shown document, landed as one perform), copy badge via playtestHover plus a flagsChanged/mouse watch that re-asserts NSCursor.dragCopy, which other views reset in the same turn. The copy's preview carries no sound: its sound needed a new bottom row, the dock grows upward, and the rows slid under the hand and aimed the drop at another track (found in the walk's mid-drag capture). New walk claims: waitFor clipsOfOneRecording / clipCopyBadge.

left rough (no task, below the bar or covered by the audit's evaluate questions): overwrite vs new track for a covering copy is the user's call in the audit; the copy's sound shows only on let go; Option-drag of several picked clips is built (each gets a copy) but no walk drives it; a copied piece keeps its clip's animated keyframes on the layer's own clock, untested for a piece copied from late in a clip.

Option-drag on a timeline clip (or one piece of a cut clip) carries out a copy and leaves the original; covering copies go onto a new track over their own; copy badge on the pointer; one undo. Core ClipDragCopy.swift + 15 tests, app EditorState+ClipBar.
